title: Our Times Are in Thy Hand, and Thou
description: Our Times Are in Thy Hand, and Thou in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 520 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Our Times are in thy Hand”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Our times are in thy hand, and thou Wilt guide our foot-steps at thy will: Lord, to thy pur-po-ses we bow, Do thou thy pur-po-ses ful-fil!

lines: Our times are in thy hand, and thou
Wilt guide our footsteps at thy will:
Lord, to thy purposes we bow,
Thy spirit guides them as they roll;
And waves on waves impetuous throng
At thy command, at thy control.
Lord, we, thy children, look to thee,
And with an humble, prostrate will,
A claim to love and serve thee still.

licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
